question: Will Senegal's National Assembly be dissolved before January 1, 2027?

calls.reasoning: Article 87 bars dissolution until Dec 2, 2026 (Assembly installed Dec 2, 2024), so the window is Dec 2-31. The standoff is acute: Pastef (130/165 seats), led by Assembly president Sonko after his May 2026 firing as PM, rejected the 2026 revised budget (Nov 3) and the first part of the 2027 budget (Nov 18, 128-18). Faye enacted the revised budget by decree on Nov 19, and Pastef is floating a high-treason resolution or a censure motion. Faye's Kiiraay camp and some ministers are calling for dissolution on Dec 2, and Faye 'does not exclude' it. Against that: his spokesman calls it a 'risky bet' and points to Article 52 as an alternative; an internal poll reportedly shows Pastef winning about 59%; he can decree budgets under Article 68; he is reportedly exploring reconciliation; and he could dissolve later in 2027, outside the window. No human market found.
calls.reference_class: Presidents facing a hostile legislative majority once a dissolution ban lifts (including Faye's own Sept 2024 dissolution at first opportunity): share that dissolve within the first month of eligibility

calls.reasoning: The Article 87 lock lifts on 2 Dec 2026, leaving a ~4-week window. The deadlock is severe: Faye dismissed Sonko in May, Sonko now runs the Pastef-controlled Assembly (130/165), it rejected the revised 2026 budget and the 2027 budget, and Faye imposed the revised budget by decree on 19 Nov. Signals for YES: Kiiraay is demanding dissolution, local elections were effectively postponed with reports Faye asked the Constitutional Council about combining them with snap legislative elections, and Faye dissolved the last Assembly on the first legal day in 2024. Signals against: Faye's party is new and could lose to Pastef, minister Camara (21 Nov) publicly called dissolution a risky bet and said 2 Dec imposes no obligation, Faye says no date is set, Article 68 lets him run budgets by decree, and there are IMF, cost and violence concerns. He could also wait until 2027. No dissolution announced as of 24 Nov. No human prediction market found.
calls.reference_class: Semi-presidential executives facing a hostile legislature majority at the moment the constitutional dissolution lock expires, dissolving within the following ~4 weeks

calls.reasoning: Article 87 only allows dissolution from 2 Dec 2026 (legislature installed 2 Dec 2024), leaving a ~30-day window. Faye and Sonko have split for good: Sonko was fired as PM in May and now leads the Assembly, Pastef expelled Faye on 17 Nov, the Assembly rejected the revised 2026 budget and the first part of the 2027 budget, and Faye enacted the 2026 budget by decree on 19 Nov. Pointing to Yes: he dissolved at the earliest legal date in 2024, reportedly asked the Constitutional Council about combining local and legislative elections, has held back the local-elections decree, his Kiraay camp is lobbying for dissolution, and his spokesman hinted at other options. Pointing to No: he says there is no fixed plan, two of his ministers warn of cost and the risk of losing to a popular Pastef, decree powers cover the budget, and he could wait until 2027. No human prediction market found.
calls.reference_class: Senegalese/francophone semi-presidential presidents facing a hostile legislative majority once the constitutional dissolution bar lifts (Faye 2024 dissolved at first opportunity; cohabitation-avoidance cases)
